title: Deuxième série de questions de Tim Burchett aux témoins

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I'm going to direct this, I believe, to Mr. Grusch, but if any of you all feel like you need to jump in, just jump right in. We're good. Has the US. Government become aware of actual evidence of extraterrestrial, otherwise unexplained forms of intelligence? And if so, when do you think this first occurred?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I like to use the term non-human. I don't like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open, both scientifically, certainly, like I've discussed publicly previously, 1930s.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Can you give me the names and titles of the people with direct firsthand knowledge and access to some of this crash retrieval some of these crash retrieval programs and maybe which facilities, military bases that the recovered material would be in. And I know a lot of congress talked about we're going to go to Area 51, and there's nothing there anymore anyway, and we move like a glacier as soon as we announce it. I'm sure the moving vans would pull up, but please.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can't discuss that publicly, but I did provide that information both to the intel committees and the Inspector General.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And we could get that in the <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr>. If we were allowed to get in a <abbr title="Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility">SCIF</abbr> with you, would that be probably what you would think?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Sure. If you had the appropriate accesses, yeah.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What special access programs cover this information, and how is it possible that they have evaded oversight for so long?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I do know the names. Once again, I can't discuss that publicly. And how they've evaded oversight in a closed setting, I could tell you the specific tradecraft use.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: All right. When do you think those programs began and who authorized them?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I do know a lot of that information, but that's something I can't discuss publicly because since...

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: All right, if any of you all want to jump in on any of this, you're more than welcome. To what level of security clearance is required to fully access these programs?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Well, anybody who has...

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: ...and I say that because myself, representative Gates, and Representative Luna were basically turned away at one point at Eglin. So please go right ahead.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Certainly difference between member access and, say, somebody like me, but anybody who has a TSSCI clearance and meets the eligibility criteria, the access adjudicative authority should be able to grant you access.

segments.speaker: Gaetz
segments.text: Mr. Burchett, if you'll yield. So just to put a fine point on that: there's nothing that you're aware of that's above special access program classification?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: It's a misnomer that there's anything actually above top secret executive order 13 526 delineates the classification levels.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Right, but I draw a point on that because we can have access to those programs, and so the notion that we're not being given that access sort of defies our typical muscle memory here in Congress. Thank you, Mr. Birch. I'll yield back to you.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Gates. Along those lines, title Ten, you may not know this or not, but title Ten and title 50 authorization. They seem to say they're inefficient. So who gets to decide this, in your opinion? In the past?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The group of career senior executive officials.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Are they government officials?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Both in and out.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do what?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Both in and out of government. And that's about as far as I got you there.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: All right, well, that leads to my next question. Which private corporations are directly involved in this program? How much taxpayer money has been invested in these programs, to your knowledge? We know we audit the Pentagon every year, and I've been here five years. And they failed the Dadgum thing every year. They lose over a billion dollars a year, we think, and I've told Department of Defense maybe 60% of their assets are unaccounted for, whatever the heck that means in the public sector. You go to jail for that kind of crap. So tell me.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yeah, I know when I'm a dollar off of my DTS travel voucher, I get hammered.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: But seems like it doesn't work the other way if you sell over $600 worth of stuff on ebay now, you get a call from the IRS. So, please, what corporations?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yeah, I don't know these specific metrics towards the end of your question. The specific corporations. I did provide to the committees in specific divisions, and I spent eleven and a half hours with both intel committees.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Has there been an active US government disinformation campaign to deny the existence of unidentified aerial phenomena? And if so, why?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can't go beyond what I've already exposed publicly about that's.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. I've been told to ask you what that... what that is, and how to get it in the record.

segments.speaker: LunaAnnaPaulina
segments.text: What have you stated publicly in your interviews for the Congressional Record?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: If you reference my News Nation interview and I talk about a multidecade campaign to disenfranchise public interest, basically.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I apologize, Mr. Chairman. I yield back negative 21 seconds.
